grades.quote: a thread’s usage increases while it runs and decays exponentially while it waits. This causes the priority to decrease while running and increase while waiting.
grades.reason: Directly explains decay-usage scheduling: usage rises while running (lowering priority) and decays exponentially while waiting (restoring priority toward base), so a thread that waited ends up with higher priority than one that recently ran.
Bibliographic notes on scheduling. They mention decay usage scheduling only in passing, in the context of proportional-share scheduling, and don't explain why a waiting thread is favored.
Says decay usage schedulers are poor at achieving proportional-share goals. It doesn't address why a waking thread is favored over a recently running one.
Describes the xv6 sleep/wakeup interface and lost wake-ups. It says nothing about decay-usage priority or usage-based priority changes.
